Not sure if we came on a good night or if others just had an off-experience. We, like many others, stumbled here instead of waiting an hour or more for Neyow's to seat our party of 3. Sounds like that happens a LOT. The hostess was outside when we walked in, but another gentleman sat us quickly. There were probably half the tables full. We sat by the window, and were greeted by our server who was definitely on the "short" side - her greeting was quick and she didn't have any "love" oozing out of her like other servers we'd had on this visit. Also she looked a little sketchy. However, that was the ONLY weirdness here. We ordered the seafood dip to share, and a cup of crawfish bisque to sha...

I have to admit I ended up here only because of the long wait at Neyow's, but I'm so glad we came here because Bayou Bistro was one of the best restaurants I found on my trip to New Orleans. The crab cake appetizer was very good, but the standouts were the crawfish etouffee and jambalaya. The etouffee was simply the best I've ever had. The roux tasted very complex and was perfectly spiced. My local friend (who I might add is a superb cook) said the jambalaya was perfect, and I echoed his sentiments; it was the best jambalaya I've ever tasted and way better than any other jambalaya I had on my visit.
